newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm in line with overseas markets.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm in line with overseas markets.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed in thin trade on Tuesday in line with international markets as the focus remained on sterling strength, dealers said.

"We are looking quite good on the back of a good backdrop in Europe and the States. Good overseas buying pushed the Irish market ahead from this morning... but we are still not out-performing German bunds or UK gilts," one dealer said.
The dealer said market focus is likely to remain on sterling strength over the short-term.

By 1610 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 had risen 45p from Monday's close at 106.10 to yield 6.12 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had risen 83p from the close at 107.45 to yield 6.81 percent.

Dealers said the release of industrial orders, which fell by 3.6 percent in September against August, had been the major factor behind the day's gains in Germany as it had ignited covering of short positions among traders who had bet Bunds were headed lower.
U.S. analysts said Treasuries extended early gains in heavy morning trade as players rushed to the market on hopes that the outcome of the presidential election will produce a split government.
